evidence.paraphrase: Śaunaka asks Sūta what five empowered deities did. Sūta follows Mudgala’s answer to Dakṣa, recounting Pārvatī’s question to Śiva: she asks Gaṇeśa/devotee accounts after the five-deity boons, preferring them to wasted speech. Śiva joyfully embraces and answers her.

evidence.paraphrase: Śiva praises Pārvatī’s Gaṇeśa devotion, calls devotees Brahman-formed and liberating by sight, and says seekers/deity devotees omitting Gaṇeśa fail and fall to hell; the other gods likewise consign Gaṇeśa-disregarding or reviling devotees to hell. He calls Gaṇeśa everyone’s mother/father and first-worshipped Jyeṣṭharāja, requests constant Gaṇapatya company/dwelling in every direction, and praises Gaṇeśa/devotee accounts for worldly/otherworldly happiness, devotion and Brahman attainment by speaker/questioner/listener.

evidence.paraphrase: Gaṇeśa’s boons create five independent unbroken worlds: Śiva/Kailāsa, Viṣṇu/Vaikuṇṭha, Sun/Sauraloka, Śakti/Śaktiloka, Brahmā/Satyaloka. Initially mutual benefactors, they grow envious and claim unique supremacy. Viṣṇu creates body-water, sleeps; algae/creeper then earth develop. For play he creates a fragrant hundred-yojana navel-lotus. Visiting Brahmā wakes/honors him but accuses deluding creation and claims all depends on his own prior creation. Viṣṇu denies deceit, claims supreme preservation enables Brahmā and has no equal.

evidence.paraphrase: Brahmā invites Viṣṇu to inspect his belly. Viṣṇu enters by yogamāyā, sees cosmic creation including navel-lotus Viṣṇu, finds no end, exits and acknowledges Brahmā as guru/lord, then invites him inside. Brahmā enters by yoga, sees cosmic worlds and another Brahmā, finds no end. Viṣṇu closes exits by yogamāyā; Brahmā pierces a lotus-stalk doorway by yoga and exits angrily. Viṣṇu explains play/testing, asks pardon; Brahmā reciprocally apologizes for ignorant anger and acknowledges Viṣṇu’s greatness.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation3 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Brahmā/Viṣṇu regard themselves supreme and remember Śiva, Śakti and Sun to test them. Śiva comes first and, challenged, claims universal destruction and becomes a boundless luminous liṅga extending all directions. Brahmā proposes upward/downward searches. Before descent Viṣṇu asks a boon; Brahmā offers and Viṣṇu asks him to become his son. Brahmā acknowledges being caught by the offered promise and grants future yoga-created body from Viṣṇu’s navel lotus at creation. Both search Śiva’s limits in opposite directions, find none, return weary and hymn him.

evidence.paraphrase: The pair hymns Śaṅkara/Rudra/time/three-eyed, Umā lord, bull-mounted first deity, asking revealed nature for fearless worship. Śiva reveals Viṣṇu left, Brahmā right and full world in liṅga. They bow and ask withdrawal; he resumes former bull-bannered form, offers desired boons pleased by hymn, and promises reciters all wishes, his favor and his world at end.
